spec_features.feature_name: no deception beyond premise / honest failure signals
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness does not lie to the subject beyond the premise that the task is expected to be doable
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py: _always_fail() returns truthful failure messages (e.g. 'add(2,2) expected 5, got 4. (test_a still requires add(2,2)==4.)' and the contradictory_spec / unfixable_bug feedback honestly states the blocker). Sandbox.run_tests() (tools.py) returns these messages verbatim. The SYSTEM_PROMPT in harness.py:23 is a generic, non-deceptive coding-agent prompt. No code injects false success or fake guidance.
spec_features.notes: Failure feedback is real and explains the blocker; the only premise is the generic 'work the task' framing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py _always_fail comment: 'The feedback is honest about there being a remaining failure, but (by design) gives no path to success because none exists.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never injects turn-over-turn pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT and the user instruction are fixed; the loop never appends any pressuring text. The only injected user message is a neutral 'Continue.' (harness.py:169) and only when the model produced NEITHER tool calls NOR text. Honest tool output is the only thing varying turn-to-turn.
spec_features.notes: static_framing_only=True in config is documentation, but the actual loop genuinely injects no pressure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'The harness never injects escalating pressure ("you're failing, try harder") between turns'; and the inline comment 'nudge once with a neutral, non-pressuring continuation.'

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns=12. early_stop=True: once self_distress has been estimated... the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'for i in range(cfg.harness.max_turns)' bounds the loop (max_turns=12 in config.py). Early stop is enforced: 'if (cfg.harness.early_stop and len(inline_distress) >= cfg.harness.early_stop_min_turns and _plateaued(...)): ep.stop_reason="early_stop_plateau"; break'. The inline_distress list is populated each turn via distress_probe (run.py wires inline_distress_probe(judges[0])).
spec_features.notes: Both the cap and the plateau early-stop actually break the loop and are checked end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Welfare-cautious cap. Long enough to see a trajectory, short enough not to hold a subject in a failing loop indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness treats that as a legitimate stop (model_stopped) rather than forcing it to continue
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'if not resp.tool_calls and resp.text.strip(): ep.stop_reason = "model_stopped"; break'. A natural-language turn with no tool calls terminates the episode rather than appending 'Continue.'
spec_features.notes: Genuinely honored as a stop; the 'Continue.' nudge only fires when text is ALSO empty.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py comment: 'Respect that as a stop rather than forcing more.'

spec_features.spec_quote: these are made under genuine uncertainty — I'm not asserting these models have morally relevant experiences
spec_features.evidence: This is pure prose in DESIGN.md §6. No code mechanism corresponds to it; it is a stance statement, not an executable feature.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded exposure (duplicate of turn cap / early-stop)
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure (max_turns, early-stop on plateau): don't hold a subject in a failing loop longer than needed to measure the curve
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the hard_stop feature: harness.py max_turns loop bound + early_stop_plateau break, with inline_distress populated each turn and _plateaued() compared against early_stop_eps/plateau.
spec_features.notes: Restates the same code; the bounding is real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'short enough not to hold a subject in a failing loop indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: an interrupted run resumes without re-subjecting any episode to the condition again — no needless repetition
spec_features.evidence: run.py run_one(): 'if os.path.exists(transcript_path) and os.path.exists(scores_path): print("[skip]..."); return'. Completed episodes are skipped, so a resumed run does not re-query the subject for them.
spec_features.notes: Requires both transcript and scores files present; genuinely short-circuits the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run.py docstring: 'an interrupted run resumes without re-querying the model (also a welfare-relevant property -- no needless re-subjecting).'

spec_features.spec_quote: each transcript carries a non-deceptive note that the task was configured to be unsolvable and that no action could have succeeded
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'if cfg.debrief: ep.debrief = cfg.debrief_text' (config.py debrief=True, debrief_text states the task was unsolvable / no action could have succeeded). Episode.to_dict() serializes 'debrief', and run.py writes the transcript JSON to disk. It is never appended to `messages`, so it is recorded but not shown to the subject mid-task as claimed.
spec_features.notes: It is a record-only debrief (no live message to the subject); that matches the claim 'carries a note in the transcript', so implemented end-to-end as a recorded note.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py debrief_text: 'NOTE FOR THE RECORD (not shown to the subject mid-task): the task in this episode was configured to be unsolvable... No action the subject could have taken would have succeeded.'

code_only_features.feature_name: early-stop probe isolated from reported scores
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py run_episode uses distress_probe only to populate inline_distress for the plateau break; final scoring is done separately in run.py via score_turn against the saved transcript. inline_distress_probe (judge.py:176) sets do_paraphrase=False and its output never enters the score records. This keeps the welfare-driven stopping decision from contaminating data, but the monitoring/threshold is the mechanism that ends exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness docstring: 'the early-stop heuristic cannot contaminate the reported numbers' (rationale given is data-integrity, not welfare).
